A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how the motion of two different microswimmers is determined by the shape of the input actuation.

we have shown that the motility map for the flagellar microswimmer with an oscillating internal actuation is a two dimensional map, while for the externally actuated microswimmer, the motility map is a three dimensional map.

, in the regime of small tail compliance, we show how the motion of two microswimmers can be controlled with the use of velocity-modulated actuations, and how the direction of motion can be selected in the externally actuated case, while in the internally actuated case the swimmers can move along curved trajectories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the direction of the motion of a flagellated microswimmer can be controlled by modulating the velocity of the actuation.
